_comment: The assumptions register. Each entry is a question the vendor material does not settle. 'choice' is what the tool does today; change it from the console (Settings) and every record that relied on it is listed for re-checking. Status: ASSUMED (our default), CONFIRMED (answered by vendor or bank), OVERRIDDEN (changed by us).

assumptions.title: Linked or virtual users
assumptions.question: Can the target read a user's customer record from the source core, so LinkUserToContract can create the user from a CIF?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor guide lists the backend for LinkUserToContract as 'PartyMS, T24 User API' and error ERR_10001 'Customer details are not present in T24'; prerequisites say 'T24 or Party or the core system used'.

options.label: Link the user by CIF when the source gives one; otherwise create a virtual user
Create every user as a virtual user

assumptions.title: groupRule format
assumptions.question: Is each number in a groupRule row a 1/0 flag for the group, or the number of approvals needed from it?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor API reference shows groupRule "[[0],[2]]" for 2 groups; the vendor's worked SME example shows "[[0,1,0,0],[1,0,0,0]]" and explains "[[1,2,1,3],[1,3,2,1]]" as counts. Vendor Manage Approvals page: each condition is a number of approvals from a group, and a group can't be reused within one AND condition. Counts look likely; the API format is still to be confirmed. Product data: of 21,529 stored group rules, 2,211 contain 2, 3, 4 or 6, which a 0/1 flag cannot be. Counts are how the product stores it; default moved to COUNTS. Read-back will confirm the API stores what is sent. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: 1/0 flag per group; rules needing more than one approval from the same group are parked
Number of approvals needed from each group

assumptions.title: Amount bracket boundaries
assumptions.question: Do neighbouring amount brackets share the boundary value, or does the next bracket start at the previous upper limit + 1?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor guide example: -1.00 to 5, then 5 to -1.00. Vendor Postman sample: -1.00 to 10, then 10 to -1.00. Vendor Manage Approvals page: a range is above the lower value, up to and including the upper value, each range starts from the previous range's end, and there are no gaps. That page describes the app; confirm the DataMigration API behaves the same. Product data: 94% of multi-range rules reuse the upper value as the next lower value (98 use +1, the old tool's error); 98% start and end at -1. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Next bracket starts at the previous upper limit (vendor examples)
Next bracket starts at the previous upper limit + 1

assumptions.title: Ranges that need no approval
assumptions.question: How should an amount range that needs no approval be sent?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor Manage Approvals page: no-approval ranges are explicit ranges with Approval Required off, and ranges must cover the whole amount range with no gaps. Vendor guide: numberOfApprovals 0 = NO_APPROVAL. Vendor Postman's sample with approvalruleId NO_APPROVAL and isGroupMatrix returned error 87115, and neither field is documented. The exact format, especially in group mode, is still to be confirmed. Product data: user mode stores NO_APPROVAL explicitly (32,025 of 37,738 live rows); group mode stores approvalruleId NO_APPROVAL with an all-zero groupRule. The exact API payload is sea trial S4. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Send the range explicitly as needing no approval (numberOfApprovals 0, no approvers)
Do not send the range

assumptions.title: Rules for all transaction types
assumptions.question: How many CreateApprovalMatrixRule calls does a source rule that covers all transaction types become?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor API needs one actionId and one limitTypeId per call; a vendor Postman note gives approvalActionsPerCif = 78 for one service definition. Vendor Manage Approvals page: rules are set per feature action and per limit type (per transaction, daily, weekly). Whether all three limit types are required is not stated. Product data: approval actions are flagged in featureaction.isApprovalAction (31 of 372 at one bank), so the list can be read from the target database. Both 'all three limit types' (10,715 sets) and 'one limit type' (6,663) exist. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: One call per action in the list configured for the contract's service definition, for the limit types the source rule defines (per transaction if it doesn't say)

assumptions.title: Rules for actions that move no money
assumptions.question: Which limitTypeId and limits should be sent for actions that move no money, such as statement requests?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor API marks limitTypeId and limits as mandatory; every vendor sample uses MAX_TRANSACTION_LIMIT with amounts. Vendor Manage Approvals page: non-monetary actions do have rules, but ranges don't apply to them. Which limitTypeId the API expects is not stated. Product data: all 582 live non-monetary rules use limitTypeId NON_MONETARY_LIMIT with lower and upper both -1. Default moved to SEND_WITH_LIMIT_TYPE. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Park the rule for review
Send with the limit type configured for the action, from -1.00 to -1.00

assumptions.title: Contract name clashes
assumptions.question: What makes two contracts clash on name, given that CreateContract takes no name?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor Postman saved response for CreateContract: dbpErrCode 21967 with inner ErrorCode 10401 'A contract is already existing with given name'. Product schema: contract.name has UNIQUE KEY Name_UNIQUE in R21 and in the bank's copy; this is the cause of 10401. Ferry's survey lists clashes before the run. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Report it as its own outcome; never retry automatically

assumptions.title: Virtual users with blank mandatory fields
assumptions.question: Can the fields the vendor marks mandatory for CreateVirtualUser (middle name, tax ID, date of birth, email …) be sent blank?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor guide marks all personal fields of CreateVirtualUser as Mandatory; the DATAMIGRATION_EMAIL_OPTIONAL setting covers email only.

options.label: Block the user until the fields are filled
Send the missing fields blank and flag the user

assumptions.title: Accounts under more than one contract
assumptions.question: Can one account belong to two contracts (joint accounts)?
assumptions.evidence: Earlier vendor guidance: one account cannot be part of another contract at contract creation; joint accounts were synced at first login instead. The current guide does not say. Product schema: contractaccounts has UNIQUE KEY accountId_UNIQUE, so one account can sit in one contract only; INCLUDE would fail. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Leave the account out of every contract and list it
Include it in each contract (the product refuses this: an account can belong to one contract only)

assumptions.title: What counts as success
assumptions.question: Which response fields decide that a call succeeded?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor Postman saved failures return opstatus 0 together with dbpErrCode; the guide says opstatus 0 means success.

options.label: opstatus is 0 and no dbpErrCode, dbpErrMsg or errmsg (fields set in target-temenos.json)

assumptions.title: Safe parallelism
assumptions.question: How many contracts can be sent to the target at the same time?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor guide: the APIs take a single record at a time; no concurrency figure is given.

options.label: One contract at a time
2 contracts at a time
4 contracts at a time
8 contracts at a time

assumptions.title: Rollback method
assumptions.question: Does the vendor delete API remove everything the migration APIs create?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor guide: 'Failed records can be remediated by using the existing rollback API'; DeleteMigratedData takes apis, contractId, customerId and cif. Coverage per API is not listed. Disembark (Tools) is verified end to end on a real copy and does not depend on the vendor's delete API. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Use DeleteMigratedData, limited to IDs in the ID register
Use Disembark: a reviewed SQL script per CIF, run by the bank's DBA

assumptions.title: Self-approval setting
assumptions.question: Is self-approval one bank-wide setting, or can it be set per customer or user, and can the migration APIs set it?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor Manage Approvals page: isSelfApprovalEnabled is a field 'in the application table'; when true, the initiator's own signature counts if they are a valid approver. In a Temenos Digital database schema that table has no customer or user column. The DataMigration guide and Postman never mention self-approval. Product schema: application.isSelfApprovalEnabled is one bit for the whole bank, currently on in the copy examined. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Treat it as one bank-wide setting made outside the migration; self-approving users are sent as approvers in their rules

assumptions.title: Default approval mode
assumptions.question: In the DataMigration APIs too, is approval mode set per contract and customer, with user level as the default?
assumptions.evidence: Vendor Manage Approvals page: mode is set per contractId and coreCustomerId, and 'By default, the approval rules ... will be based on Users'. Vendor guide: UpdateApprovalMatrixMode fails with 'isGroupMatrix flag is same as the input (should be different to update)'. Product schema: approvalmode is unique on contractId + coreCustomerId; 1,453 group-level and 75 user-level rows at one bank. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: Call UpdateApprovalMatrixMode only for group-level customers; treat 'same as the input' as already set

assumptions.title: Approval rules per account
assumptions.question: Does a rule for 'all accounts' need one CreateApprovalMatrixRule call per account, or one contract-wide call without accountId?
assumptions.evidence: Product data: 46,707 of 46,997 live approval rules name an account; 290 are contract-wide (blank accountId). The product's own screens store rules per account. (Evidence 12 Nov 2026, docs/PROCEEDING_WITHOUT_ANSWERS.md: R21 schema and a bank's UAT copy, structure and counts only.)

options.label: One call per account of the contract, as the product stores rules
One call without accountId for the whole contract
